steps.rationale: Minimal depth; Slice 2 hook runner covered by fixture matrix.

counterexamples: A hook preserves parseability but changes ordered-list or scalar-type semantics.
A hook succeeds once but emits different bytes on a second pass, breaking idempotence assumptions.
A malicious or misconfigured hook rewrites files outside project-owned ./tied/.
Agents invoke a hook without repository declaration because MCP exposes an implicit default formatter.
falsification_questions: Can a second hook pass change bytes while still semantically equivalent?
Can semantic drift pass when post-hook YAML parses cleanly?
Can the hook run on tied/methodology/** when declared?
disconfirming_observations: Invalid client_formatter schema fails at resolve time without running the hook.
Path guard tests reject methodology paths and paths outside tiedBasePath.
yaml_semantic_compare runs between pre-hook snapshot and post-hook bytes before acceptance.
